extDescription.message: Highlight text and add private notes on any website. Everything stays on your device.

orphanHint.message: This text is no longer on the page, or the page hasn't finished loading.

emptyUnsupportedText.message: Browser pages and extension stores can't be annotated. Open any website to start.

emptyPageTitle.message: No notes on this page yet

emptyPageText.message: Select some text, click the small button at its end and pick a color, or right-click and choose “Highlight and add a note”.

emptySearchText.message: Try a different phrase or clear the filters.

emptyAllTitle.message: Your notes will show up here

emptyAllText.message: Highlight text on any website to create your first note.

emptyPageGoneText.message: They may have been deleted. Go back to see your other pages.

settingToolbarHint.message: A small button at the end of selected text that opens the colors.

settingStyleHint.message: How highlighted text looks on websites.

settingDefaultColorHint.message: Used for notes created from the menu.

privacyText.message: Your highlights and notes stay on-device and will never leave your browser.

navAllSubtitle.message: Everything you've highlighted, across all websites.

confirmDeleteText.message: The highlight will disappear from the page. This can't be undone.

settingSite.message: Turn Annotator off on this site

settingSiteDisable.message: Turn Annotator off on this site

settingSiteAppHint.message: Annotator is off by default on web apps

cmd_highlight_note.message: Highlight the selection and add a note

cmd_toggle_panel.message: Show or hide the notes panel

actionReanchorHint.message: Select the new text on the page first, then click to pin this note to it

panelOpenHint.message: Show the notes panel on this page

panelEmpty.message: No highlights here yet. Select some text to create one.

panelOrphansHint.message: The text may have changed. Select its new version on the page and click “Pin to selection”.

pageNoteAdd.message: Add a note about the whole page

toastImportedNothing.message: Nothing new in this file — everything is already here

toastImportInvalid.message: This isn't an Annotator backup file

toastReanchored.message: Note pinned to the new text

toastReanchorNoSelection.message: Select the new text on the page first

shortcutToolbarKeysHint.message: 1–9 pick a category by position, a category's own key works too, / searches the list, N adds a note.

shortcutChangeHint.message: Shortcuts are set in the browser's extension settings.

dataBackupHint.message: Save your notes as JSON (a full backup you can import again), or as Markdown or CSV for reading and analysis.

whatsNewShort.message: Side panel, keyboard shortcuts, your own categories and backups.

whatsNewPanel.message: A side panel on every page with your highlights, a page note and notes whose text has moved.

whatsNewShortcuts.message: Keyboard shortcuts, formatting in notes, and copying quotes with a link.

whatsNewCategories.message: Your own categories: name the colors after what you mark, add more and give each a key.

whatsNewBackup.message: Backups you can import on another device, and Markdown export.

whatsNewFiles.message: Save highlights into your HTML files (Export → HTML files), so Git can track them.

readerViewHint.message: You're in Reader View. Highlights show and can be added on the original page.

exportEmpty.message: There is nothing to export in this selection.

exportJsonHint.message: A full backup with colors, categories and notes. The only format you can import back.

exportMarkdownHint.message: A readable document with colors, dates and links. Good for sharing, Obsidian, Notion or GitHub.

exportCsvHint.message: One row per highlight: page, color, text, note and dates. Opens in Excel, Google Sheets and LibreOffice.

exportHtmlHint.message: Writes highlights and notes into the files themselves, so Git can track them and nothing depends on the browser's storage. Files on your computer only.

exportSeparatorHint.message: If Excel puts everything in one column, choose the other separator.

exportCsvFormulaHint.message: Text that starts with = + - or @ gets a leading apostrophe, so Excel never runs it as a formula.

exportHtmlSteps.message: Next you choose the folder that holds the files, or a folder above it. Only the notes are added to them; the rest of each file stays exactly as it was.

exportHtmlStepsDownload.message: Next you choose the folder that holds the files, or a folder above it. Firefox can't write into folders, so the updated files come as a zip to copy over the originals.

exportHtmlScope.message: Local files here: $V1$. Each one gets all of its notes, and anything an earlier save wrote into it is replaced.

exportHtmlEmpty.message: None of these notes are on local files. Only files on this computer can be updated.

toastExportFailed.message: Couldn't create the export. Try again.

toastBurnFailed.message: Couldn't save into the files. Try again.

burnDownloaded.message: Files updated: $V1$, downloaded as a zip.

burnDownloadedHint.message: Copy them over the originals. Inside the zip each one keeps its folder.

burnUpToDate.message: Everything was already up to date.

burnUnplaced.message: Notes that could not be marked in the text because it is no longer there: $V1$. They are still saved in the files.

burnSkipped.message: Left alone because they are not UTF-8 text ($V1$):

burnNothing.message: Nothing to save: none of these notes are on local files.

fileAccessTitle.message: Is this a file on your computer?

fileAccessBadge.message: Annotator: local files need one more setting. Click for details.

fileAccessText.message: Chrome keeps extensions out of pages saved on your computer until you allow it. Open Annotator's settings, turn on “Allow access to file URLs”, then reload the page.

settingFileAccessOn.message: Annotator works on HTML files saved on your computer.

settingFileAccessOff.message: Chrome blocks Annotator on files saved on your computer. Turn on “Allow access to file URLs” in the extension's settings.

fileAccessTextFirefox.message: Firefox keeps extensions out of pages saved on your computer until you allow it. Open about:addons, choose Annotator, then on the “Permissions and data” tab turn on “Access local files on your computer” (not “Run on sites with restrictions”, that's a different switch) and reload the page.

settingFileAccessOffFirefox.message: Firefox blocks Annotator on files saved on your computer. In about:addons, open Annotator's “Permissions and data” tab and turn on “Access local files on your computer” (not “Run on sites with restrictions”).

toastFileAccessCopied.message: Copied. Paste it into the address bar.

pdfText.message: Your browser opens PDFs in its own viewer, which extensions can't reach. Notes work on web pages and on HTML files saved on your computer.

pdfBadge.message: Annotator: PDFs open in the browser's own viewer, which extensions can't reach.

dataRelocateHint.message: Notes belong to a page's address or file path. If you moved files to another folder or drive, or a site changed its address, point your notes at the new location.

relocateIntro.message: Enter where the pages used to be and where they are now. A folder, a network path or a web address all work. Tip: copy the path from your file manager or the browser's address bar.

relocateHint.message: Notes under the old location will be moved to the new one.

relocateInvalid.message: That doesn't look like a folder, file or web address.

relocateNone.message: No notes found at the old location.

relocateSame.message: The old and new locations are the same.

relocateMerge.message: Notes already exist for $V1$ of them at the new location; those will be combined.

relocateReminder.message: Your files are not touched. Only the addresses your notes are stored under change.

toastRelocateFailed.message: Couldn't move the notes. Try again.

categoriesIntro.message: Name your colors after what you mark (for example “Sample size” or “Outcome”), add more, and give each a key. With quick keys on, select text and press the key to highlight it in that category. Exports use these names.

categoryKeyHint.message: A letter or digit. Select text and press it to highlight in this category (needs quick keys).

categoryKeyInvalid.message: A key must be a single letter or digit.

categoryDeleteMove.message: In this category: $V1$. Move them to:

settingQuickKeysHint.message: Select text, then press a category's key to highlight it right away. Works only on selected text outside text fields.

confirmDeleteUndoText.message: The highlights disappear from their pages. You can still undo it right after.

categoryResetText.message: Their names, colors and keys go back to the originals. Your own categories stay as they are.

settingSitePdf.message: This is a PDF: Annotator can't run here.

exportIncludeSettingsHint.message: Appearance, quick keys and per-site rules. Importing the file applies them on the other device.

guideIntro.message: Highlight what matters on any page, add your notes and find it all later. Everything stays on this device.

guideTryHint.message: Nothing on this page is saved, so try anything. Your categories and keys work here as everywhere else.

guideDemo1.message: Good notes start with careful reading. Select this sentence, click the small button at its end and pick a color: that's a highlight.

guideDemo2.message: Now try a shortcut: select any part of this paragraph and press the one shown on the left. With the color bar open, the digits 1–9 pick a category too.

guideDemo3.message: Click a highlight to write a note about it or to change its color. Then open the side panel to see everything you marked on this page in one list.

guideStepHighlightText.message: Select text, click the small button at its end and pick a color. Or skip the clicking with a shortcut:

guideStepNoteText.message: Click a highlight to write a note, change its color or delete it. To highlight and start the note at once:

guideStepKeysText.message: With the color bar open, 1–9 pick a category, / searches them all and N adds a note. With quick keys on, a category's own key highlights the selection straight away.

guideStepPanelText.message: The side panel lists the page's highlights in reading order, along with a note for the whole page.

guideStepCategoriesText.message: In Settings → Categories, name the colors after what you mark, add more and give each a key.

guideStepAllText.message: All notes from every page: search, filter by category, and export to JSON, Markdown or CSV.

toastOpenFileYourself.message: Firefox doesn't let extensions open files from your computer. The file's address is copied: paste it into the address bar, and the note will show as soon as the file opens.

categoryBulkIntro.message: One name per line. You can paste a column straight from a spreadsheet. Names already in use are skipped.

categoryDrag.message: Drag to reorder (or use the arrow keys)
